newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on cash support.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on cash support.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps edged up at midday on Wednesday on extended support in the physical market amid firmer overnight crude values, traders said.
"Gas oil firmed slightly this morning because of the physical buying yesterday," said a trader.
May gas oil swaps were last quoted $25.20/$25.40 per barrel, up about 10 cents from Tuesday's quotes in quiet trading.
Traders said apart from the overnight 10 cents rise to June Brent crude, the market was also boosted by the emergence of a new buyer in the physical market.
The buyer, a Chinese trader who has storage facilites in Malaysia, bought a 150,000-barrel cargo from a European major at $25.15 per barrel for loading June 1-5.

On top of this, two 150,000-barrel cargoes were sold to a local trader at $25.50 per barrel. The same trader together with two other traders have bought almost 19 million barrels of gas oil since March 3.
Traders said these actions suggest that there is strong support in the physical market at the $25.00 mark and the swaps market is taking its cue from these moves.
Fuel oil swaps gave up some of its Tuesday gains as the market corrected a more than $2.00 per barrel one-day hike in prices.
On Tuesday, May swaps traded to a high of $100.50 per tonne on expectations of tight supplies.
But the market eased this morning after physical sellers emerged with a 20,000-tonne cargo traded at $100.00 per tonne for end May/early June loading.
May swaps were last quoted at $99.50/$101.50 per tonne down from Tuesday's $100.25/$101.00, brokers said.
